extracted.intended_audience: small businesses, small non-profits, and local governmental jurisdictions who want to engage with federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Practical steps small entities can take to influence federal regulations: report harmful rules, attend listening sessions, submit comment letters, request meetings with regulators, and follow Advocacy for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report regulatory problems via the Red Tape Hotline
rubrics_metrics.description: We can help you cut through the red tape strangling your business. Contact the Red Tape Hotline for a direct way to report federal regulations that hurt your ability to grow, compete, or innovate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact methods: email RedTape@sba.gov, call 800-827-5722 and select Option 3, or complete the online form. Use this channel to report specific federal regulations that are harming your business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend a Virtual Roundtable / listening session
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy attorneys set up routine listening sessions where small businesses can speak directly with staff members from federal agencies who write rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These roundtables are hosted virtually and are an opportunity to ask questions and share concerns directly with agencies and Advocacy staff. Check the 'view roundtable events' listing to find sessions to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a comment letter to federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: You can participate in the rulemaking process by writing a comment letter directly to federal agencies. Agencies consider quality comments, and a good letter can help shape regulations that impact your business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Advocacy’s 'Small Business Guide to Comment Letter Writing' to make the process easier. Emphasis: don’t be intimidated; focus on producing a quality comment that clearly explains the impact on your business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule and attend a 12866 meeting with regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: You can meet directly with federal regulators and tell them your story. These meetings, called 12866 meetings, give you an uninterrupted thirty minutes to talk with representatives of the federal government about how a rule might impact your business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to explain concrete impacts during the 30-minute, uninterrupted meeting. Use the 'learn more' resource to understand how to request and make the most of a 12866 meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Office of Advocacy for timely updates
rubrics_metrics.description: You can follow Advocacy on LinkedIn, X, or Facebook for timely updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow those social channels to receive announcements about regulatory alerts, roundtables, comment opportunities, and other Advocacy activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide input for the 'Small Businesses’ Most Wanted Reform' list
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important issues Advocacy tracks are on the Small Businesses’ Most Wanted Reform page. In order to determine which regulations go on this page, we need your input!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit examples and input about high-priority regulatory problems so Advocacy can prioritize and publicize reforms that affect small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for Advocacy-issued regulatory alerts
rubrics_metrics.description: When an opportunity arises to work with an agency, Advocacy staff issues a regulatory alert to notify small businesses and solicit comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign up for or monitor alerts so you can respond quickly to solicitations for comments and participate in shaping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for regulatory flexibility where one-size-fits-all rules fail
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy pushes for flexibility where one-size-fits-all regulations will not work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments or speaking with regulators, emphasize alternatives or exemptions that provide needed flexibility for small entities rather than blanket rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on regulations that increase costs in critical industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy reviews regulations that have driven up prices in industries including housing, healthcare, and energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your concern relates to cost impacts in these or similar industries, highlight concrete price or cost-increase effects in your communications to help Advocacy evaluate and escalate the issue.
